title: Oxygen on the 26.5 isopycnal of the core CalCOFI grid stopped its 1984-2006 decline and stayed low in 2007-2025; trend, salinity-proxy and new-decline forecasts failed (bottle data)
abstract: Question: did the 1984-2006 oxygen decline in the subsurface southern California Current continue, and did published forecasts work? Approach: we used Winkler bottle oxygen from the CalCOFI bottle database (to 2021-05) and from the bottle rows of CalCOFI CTD product files (2021-07 to 2025-04). The data are 9,705 casts at 57 core stations. We calculated anomalies from the 1984-2006 station x season means and tested 2007-2025 out of sample. Results: on sigma0 = 26.5, oxygen fell at -1.04 umol/kg per year in 1984-2006 (95% interval -1.39 to -0.69). In 2007-2025 the slope was +0.10 (-0.08 to +0.28), and the mean anomaly was -16.2 umol/kg. The extended 1984-2006 trend (RMSE 8.7) forecast worse than the held 2002-2006 level (RMSE 3.9), but this loss difference is marginal. A new strong decline by 2020, as Pozo Buil and Di Lorenzo (2017) predicted, did not occur: 2018-2025 oxygen was 1.8 umol/kg higher than 2008-2017 (0.1 to 3.5), and the 60 umol/kg hypoxic boundary was 11 m deeper (2 to 21). The isopycnal-salinity proxy (r = -0.92 in 1984-2006) failed after 2006 (r = -0.15). Salinity went back toward its mean, but oxygen stayed 11.5 umol/kg below the proxy (-14.4 to -9.6). Solubility explains 4% of the oxygen loss. The AOU gain matched the phosphate gain at the remineralization ratio (ratio 186, interval 158-230), and N* fell by 0.67 uM. All 57 stations lost oxygen. The results hold nearshore and offshore, on sigma0 = 26.7, without 2023, and in the bottle database alone. Limitations: post-2021 values are preliminary. We tested the local CalCOFI salinity relation, not the reanalysis index of the 2017 paper. The test record has 19 autocorrelated years. The process attribution is descriptive.

display.caption: Core CalCOFI grid (57 stations), anomalies from the 1984-2006 station x season means. Top: oxygen on sigma0 = 26.5 (gray dots are cruise means, blue line is annual means), with three forecasts for 2007-2025: the extended 1984-2006 trend (orange), the held 2002-2006 level (dotted), and the salinity proxy fit in 1984-2006 (aqua). Middle: salinity on sigma0 = 26.5. Bottom: depth anomaly of the 60 umol/kg hypoxic boundary (negative is shallower). The vertical dashed line marks the change from the bottle database to the bottle rows of the CTD product files (after 2021-05).

Annual oxygen against annual salinity on sigma0 = 26.5. Blue points are the 1984-2006 training years; the line is their OLS fit (-360 umol/kg per psu). Orange points are the 2007-2025 test years. In the test years, oxygen is 11.5 umol/kg below the fit on average and does not follow salinity (r = -0.15).

Change at each core station, 2008-2025 mean minus 1984-1995 mean. Left: oxygen on sigma0 = 26.5 (all 57 stations negative). Right: depth of the 60 umol/kg hypoxic boundary (all 56 stations with data shallower).

citations.reason: Reports the 1984-2006 CalCOFI oxygen decline and hypoxic-boundary shoaling. We extend its trend as a forecast and test it in 2007-2025.
Uses isopycnal salinity as an oxygen proxy and predicts a new strong oxygen decline by 2020. The CalCOFI 2018-2025 data show no new decline, and the local salinity-oxygen relation failed after 2006.
